title: Redwood migration demo - OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood
header: Date: 2026-01-09 / Start: 15:00 UTC / Duration: 46m - Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lucia Gomez (Redwood SE), Aaron Chen (Redwood Product), Meera Srinivasan (CTO, Stratus), Jake Morris (ML Eng), Priya Rao (Infra), Tom Kline (Security)
summary: Intro + migration demo focused on API parity (completion/chat/embeddings), Console/Optimize walkthrough, and migration playbook. Customer concerned about latency, kv cache behavior, SSO/KMS, and model-quality parity. Agreed to run a 2-week POC with throughput benchmark and security review.
topics: API parity mapping (completions vs chat vs function calls)
Console and Redwood Optimize walkthrough (batching/quantization suggestions)
Security: VPC, KMS, SOC2 and audit logs
transcript:
00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, AE at Redwood. Quick roll call?
00:07 Meera: Meera here, Stratus CTO. Jake and Priya on from infra. Tom from security might jump in with questions.
00:15 Samir: Awesome. Today we'll show API parity — how you map existing OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls to Redwood API and a bit of the Console and Optimize tooling. Lucia will drive the demo.
00:27 Lucia: Hi all, I'll share my screen—bear with me while the deck loads. So first slide is high level: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private deploy options. We map completions/chat/embeddings and function calls.
00:40 Jake: Quick Q: we currently use GPT-4o style calls with streaming and function call hooks, and a custom stop token setup. How similar will Redwood be?
00:50 Lucia: Good question. Redwood supports streaming out of the box, function/tool calling with the same JSON-ish signature, and stop sequences — in practice you'll pass the same args, a few param names differ. We have an adapter layer in our SDK to make switch minimal.
01:10 Aaron: Important note: for parity we recommend testing temperature & top_p mappings; sometimes sampling differs slightly so we run a short eval set.
01:22 Meera: Right, quality parity is critical. We need identical behavioral outputs for our chat assistant in prod.
01:28 Lucia: Totally. We do a prompt/response mapping doc — we'll share. Also Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization and batching that preserve quality targets.
01:40 Tom: On security: are audit logs available? What's retention? KMS integration?
01:46 Samir: Yes: audit logs, request-level traces in Console, and KMS/HSM integration for Private. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via cloud KMS in Dedicated/Private. Retention is configurable with add-on SLAs.
01:58 Priya: Any network requirements for Private? We have a strict VPC-only policy.
02:02 Lucia: For Private we run a control plane which you can host in VPC, with optional air-gapped on-prem setup. We support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and can bake in your VPC peering.
02:18 Meera: Cool. Demo time?
02:21 Lucia: Yep. Switching to the API console — here is a sample mapping: OpenAI completions -> POST /v1/completions on Redwood with body fields prompt/max_tokens/temperature. Chat calls map to /v1/chat with messages array; function calling is available as schema + call instructions.
02:41 Jake: Do we need to change request IDs or conversation IDs? We use conversation_id to stitch KV cache.
02:48 Lucia: You can pass conversation_id and we expose a KV cache affinity header. Our KV cache is prefix-aware; we also provide explicit cache control headers. Small naming diffs: we call it x-rw-conversation-id in the SDK, but it's trivial to wire.
03:05 Meera: How about embeddings? We use embeddings heavily for search rerank.
03:10 Lucia: Embeddings is a single endpoint, same semantics. We also provide batch embeddings and auto-batching in Redwood Optimize suggestions to help throughput.
03:20 Aaron: I want to point out that for migration we recommend a 2-week POC: import a snapshot of prompts, run parity tests, and then cutover with canary routes.
03:31 Meera: Sounds fair. What about latency — we commonly need < 120ms 95p on short responses.
03:38 Lucia: For short responses with our hosted low-latency model family you should see sub-100ms p95 in US regions for small-ish models; for high-capacity you'll want Dedicated. We'll run a perf benchmark matching your payload distribution.
03:50 Jake: Any gotchas on token counting—our billing pipelines assume OpenAI tokenization.
03:56 Aaron: Good call—there can be differences. We expose token_count in response and have a tokenizer util in the SDK to align with your internal billing; we'll include that in the adapter.
04:12 Tom: Regarding compliance: SOC2, ISO?
04:15 Samir: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and pursuing ISO 27001; for Dedicated/Private we provide audit artifacts and support for customer audits.
04:25 Priya: Great. Can you show the Console for routing and rollouts?
04:29 Lucia: Sure—Console view: per-model dashboard, latency/cost per route, rollout controls — canary percent, auto-fallback. Here is a canary we set up previously for a customer: 10% traffic, auto-failover to baseline model on regressions.
04:47 Meera: So we can route specific customers to Dedicated while others hit Hosted?
04:51 Lucia: Yes, routing by customer tier, region, or latency policy.
05:00 Jake: On optimizing cost, would you recommend quantization? We've been cautious about quantizing due to quality drift.
05:07 Aaron: Redwood Optimize will analyze your eval set and suggest quantization profiles that meet a quality delta threshold. You can also do stage quantization in Dedicated.
05:18 Meera: If results drift, what's rollback look like?
05:21 Lucia: Instant: Console rollbacks to previous quantization or model version, or auto-fallback to unquantized variant if configured.
05:29 Jake: Can we do offline AB tests? We have gold prompts and a scorer.
05:33 Aaron: Yep — we can run offline evals and surface delta metrics; the platform links regressions to prompt failures in the Console.
05:42 Tom: Security question—are logs redacted? We store request/response with options for PII scrubbing, and log redaction rules.
05:50 Samir: Correct; redaction can be configured, and for Private you control retention and scrubbing.
06:00 Meera: Let's talk timelines — we have an internal Q1 target to cut over staging. Can you support a POC starting next week?
06:06 Samir: Yes. We'll provision a Dedicated trial or hosted pilot depending on your needs. Plan: week 1 setup + parity tests; week 2 throughput and security work.
06:16 Priya: For the POC we'll need an architecture doc and a checklist for infra changes.
06:21 Lucia: We'll share a migration playbook and an SDK adapter example (Node/Python) that maps your current OpenAI/Together calls to Redwood.
06:30 Jake: Are there any differences in backpressure behavior when we hit concurrency limits? We use custom retries.
06:36 Lucia: The runtime exposes rate limit headers and queue-depth metrics; backpressure-handling best practice is in the adapter. For Dedicated, you can provision headroom and burst capacity.
06:48 Meera: Can we run a small benchmark now with a quick script?
06:51 Samir: We can kick a benchmark but we'll need your sample payloads. If you share a curl/JS snippet we'll run it in our sandbox and return p95/p50 and token costs.
07:03 Meera: I'll share a redacted sample after the call.
07:06 Jake: One more — function calling differences, sometimes we rely on tool state size, do you support streaming tool output?
07:13 Lucia: Yes, streaming tool output and partial tool results are supported; we also stream tokens for the model response so UX is preserved.
07:23 Tom: Is there any encryption at rest for embeddings? They're sensitive.
07:26 Samir: Embedding vectors stored in Dedicated/Private are encrypted with customer KMS. For Hosted, we offer encryption with provider KMS and optional bring-your-own-key for enterprise plans.
07:40 Meera: Great. Could you recap next steps?
07:43 Samir: Sure. Lucia, Aaron — quick recap?
07:46 Lucia: We'll send: 1) migration playbook + SDK adapter examples; 2) parity test template and eval harness; 3) product deck + Console screenshots.
07:56 Aaron: We'll also provision a sandbox for the benchmark and a test plan that maps your top 200 prompts.
08:02 Meera: From Stratus: we'll share sample payloads, the gold prompt set, and security questionnaire answers.
08:09 Samir: Great. I think that's it—thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with dates for POC kickoff.
08:16 Meera: Thanks all.

Note: timestamps here are approximate; recording shows about 46 minutes of discussion including Q&A and sidebars. Transcription contains occasional misheard proper nouns (e.g., Together -> "Together AI" sometimes transcribed as "To get her") and generic speaker labels.
